data.exact_reserve_text: During 2016, net ultimate claims in respect of prior underwriting years (2014 & prior) reduced by GBP 6.7m. This was mainly due to favourable claims development over the year in the Director's & Officers, Marine Liability and Aerospace classes. The Airline Liability class also benefited from a GBP 2.7m takedown in the large 2008 Air France loss. These reductions were offset by net ultimate claims increases in the A&H and General Liability classes, partly due to increased exposure estimates as inwards premium from binders were revised upwards.

data.standardized_narrative: Gross claims reserves opened at GBP 411.419m. Using the gross claims development triangle, prior-year development for underwriting years 2014 and earlier produced a net release on gross reserves of approximately GBP 11.95m (around 2.9% of opening gross reserves). The movement was driven by favourable claims development in Directors & Officers, Marine Liability and Aerospace (Aviation) and a takedown in the legacy 2008 Air France loss, partially offset by adverse movements in Accident & Health and General Liability largely driven by increased exposure estimates from binders.

data.data_quality_notes: No explicit gross 'movement in prior year's provision' note was found. A gross prior-year development figure was derived from the gross claims development triangle (comparing current estimate to the previous diagonal for UW years 2011-2014). The managing agent reports a net prior-year reduction of GBP 6.7m; that net figure is reported in the text, but the gross figure above (-GBP 11.948m) comes from the gross triangle. Some event amounts cited in the narrative are net of reinsurance; gross breakdowns by event were not provided.
